palette.role: Summer scent, pollinator interest and berries at human scale.

handedness.basis: Climbs clockwise seen from above (Wildlife Trusts; grouped with hop against bindweed in older texts): a left-handed helix. No peer-reviewed species-level source was retrieved.

attachment.supportNeeds: Guided support with sun on the upper shoots and a cooler root zone; a lane distinct from the evergreen honeysuckle.

wood.basis: A reconciliation of sources that disagree, not a published statement. For previous-season wood: Gardens Illustrated says L. periclymenum and its cultivars "flower on stems that have grown the previous year"; the RHS record says prune after flowering, and the RHS honeysuckle guide says types pruned after flowering bear flowers "on short sideshoots on the previous season's growth". For current-season wood: Bean's supplement (Trees and Shrubs Online) says 'Graham Thomas' "if cut back in winter will flower from June to October", and the RHS record notes a long flowering season. Taken together: a first flush from last year's stems, continued on new growth.

monthsUK.basis: Bean's supplement (Trees and Shrubs Online), of this cultivar: "if cut back in winter will flower from June to October". Stated in months. The RHS record names no months: its season grid shows flowers in summer only and its text says "long flowering season"; the earlier value of June to August came from that.

flowering.display: Fragrant white flowers ageing to cream-yellow over a long period; red berries.

site.aspect: Full sun or partial shade; aspect flexible; partial shade often favourable.

calendar.note: RHS pruning group 11: prune after flowering, as needed.

management.notes: Prune and control after flowering as needed; keep a lane separate from the evergreen honeysuckle.
